nextReviewTrigger: H1 exit-gate review or any change to provider, event, permission, or platform contracts

statusDefinitions.discovery: Problem and success measure are being defined.
statusDefinitions.planned: Accepted scope with dependencies and acceptance criteria.
statusDefinitions.in_progress: Implementation is active and the item is not yet through every gate.
statusDefinitions.blocked: No meaningful progress is possible until a named dependency changes.
statusDefinitions.beta: User journey works but release-quality gates remain.
statusDefinitions.done: Every acceptance criterion passes on the target platforms.
statusDefinitions.deferred: Intentionally postponed with the reason kept visible.

phases.title: Product foundation
phases.outcome: A coherent product shell with stable contracts, deterministic replay, and clean Windows/Linux build gates.
exitGates: The Svelte interface contains no provider transport or orchestration business logic.
The Rust core runs in tests without Tauri.
A recorded fake session replays into the complete task interface.
Database projections rebuild deterministically.
Clean Windows and Linux builds pass.
Architecture changes have decision records and roadmap change notes.

items.title: Product language and interactive preview
items.outcome: A user can understand Kiln's task, provider, review, and roadmap model before repository execution exists.
acceptanceCriteria: Workbench, provider onboarding, diff review, and roadmap views are interactive.
Web production build, lint, and rendered-output tests pass.
No starter branding or unused starter surface remains.
items.changeNote: Completed in the initial Kiln foundation.

items.title: Typed provider boundary
items.outcome: OpenAI, Anthropic, and a local compatible server share one normalized Rust command surface.
acceptanceCriteria: OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages, and local Chat Completions adapters compile.
Connection tests and normalized chat responses use typed request and error models.
Recorded parsing, URL-safety, and secret-redaction tests pass for all provider types.
items.changeNote: Non-streaming foundation complete; streaming remains H1.

items.title: Product specification and architecture
items.outcome: Product boundaries, safety guarantees, platform claims, and non-goals are explicit and reviewable.
acceptanceCriteria: The product specification defines launch workflows and permission semantics.
The architecture separates interface, orchestration, providers, workspace host, and storage.
Local-first control-plane decisions are recorded.
items.changeNote: Completed in revision 0.1.

items.title: Reproducible Svelte/Tauri desktop build
items.outcome: A contributor can install, check, build, and launch the native shell from a clean checkout.
acceptanceCriteria: JavaScript dependencies are locked.
Svelte type checking and production build pass.
Tauri launches the generated frontend through the typed Rust commands.
A clean Windows build passes; a clean Linux build passes in CI.
items.changeNote: Completed in revision 1.2 after clean hosted Windows and Ubuntu installs, Svelte checks, production builds, and complete Rust workspace builds passed.

items.title: Living roadmap automation
items.outcome: Repository documentation and both in-product roadmap views are generated from one reviewed source.
acceptanceCriteria: Stable roadmap data is stored in product/roadmap.json.
ROADMAP.md and web/desktop summary modules are generated from that source.
A freshness check fails when generated outputs drift.
items.changeNote: Added in revision 0.2 to eliminate roadmap duplication.

items.title: Extract the UI-independent Rust core
items.outcome: Provider, task, policy, and event behavior can run and test without Tauri.
acceptanceCriteria: kiln-core, kiln-providers, and kiln-platform crates have no Tauri dependency.
kiln-tauri contains transport and application wiring only.
Provider fixture tests run against the extracted crates.
items.changeNote: Completed in revision 0.3 with a Cargo workspace, Tauri-free core/provider/platform crates, and 15 passing extracted-crate tests.

items.title: Versioned command and event contract
items.outcome: Every task transition has a stable, serializable, causally ordered representation.
acceptanceCriteria: Project, workspace, task, session, turn, approval, tool, artifact, and receipt events are versioned.
Per-task sequence and causation identifiers are defined.
Unknown additive event fields are tolerated and breaking versions fail explicitly.
The Svelte interface consumes application events rather than provider events.
items.changeNote: Completed in revision 0.4: Rust and TypeScript contracts, deterministic Svelte projections, provider-result normalization, compatibility tests, contract documentation, and ADR 0002.

items.title: SQLite event log and deterministic projections
items.outcome: Task state survives restart and can be rebuilt from an auditable local history.
acceptanceCriteria: Events append transactionally with schema and migration versions.
Secrets and raw environment snapshots are forbidden from durable payloads.
Projection rebuilds produce stable snapshot fixtures.
Migration forward and rollback tests pass.
items.changeNote: Completed in revision 0.6 with transactional SQLite append/replay, migrations, secret rejection, close/reopen recovery, versioned projection snapshots, Tauri application-data initialization, typed storage commands, durable-before-visible Svelte batches, and startup restore.

items.title: Recorded fake-session replay
items.outcome: The complete task interface can be developed and tested without a live provider.
acceptanceCriteria: A fixture includes streaming text, a plan, a proposed tool, an approval, output, a diff, tests, and a completion receipt.
Replay produces the expected task, activity, and inspector projections.
Repeated replay is deterministic.
items.changeNote: Completed in revision 0.7 with one generated 25-event recording, rich Rust and TypeScript projection snapshots, visible desktop artifacts, and deterministic replay tests.

items.title: Windows and Linux continuous integration
items.outcome: Cross-platform claims are proved on every change.
acceptanceCriteria: Rust format, check, unit tests, and frontend freshness/build checks run on both platforms.
Fixtures cover spaces, Unicode paths, line endings, and process cancellation.
Release-blocking failures are visible before merge.
items.changeNote: Completed in revision 1.2 with green hosted Windows and Ubuntu jobs, portable generated-file and projection fixtures, and both quality jobs required by main-branch protection.

phases.title: Connected vertical slice
phases.outcome: One genuine repository task completes safely through each required provider type.
exitGates: The same fixture task completes through OpenAI, Anthropic, and a local compatible server.
Tool input and results appear in causal order.
Cancellation stops generation and execution within a documented bound.
Denied tools produce no side effect.
Every changed file is inspectable before acceptance.
Credentials never appear in events, logs, exports, or crash reports.

items.title: Normalized streaming and cancellation
items.outcome: Users see responsive provider output and can stop a turn reliably.
acceptanceCriteria: All three adapters emit normalized message deltas and completion events.
Cancellation propagates through provider HTTP and active tool jobs.
Late provider events cannot mutate a cancelled turn.
items.changeNote: Completed in revision 0.9 with normalized SSE adapters, a shared cancellation domain, ordered Tauri channels, durable desktop deltas, a stop control, late-event guards, fixtures, and ADR 0005.

items.title: Open and remember a Git repository
items.outcome: A user can select a real project and start a task against a truthful workspace state.
acceptanceCriteria: Repository identity, root, branch, status, and project defaults are projected.
Invalid or unsafe repository selections fail with actionable messages.
Remembered projects contain no credentials.
items.changeNote: Completed in revision 1.0 with a Tauri-free bounded Git inspector, typed project/workspace projections, immutable remembered-project events, live startup revalidation, actionable selection errors, credential-free defaults, a desktop project picker, and cross-language tests.

items.title: Read-only file and search tools
items.outcome: An agent can inspect a repository through typed, visible, policy-checked tools.
acceptanceCriteria: File read, file search, and text search use typed schemas.
Paths are constrained to the selected workspace.
Tool proposals and results appear in the ordered activity timeline.
items.changeNote: Completed in revision 1.1 with tagged Rust and TypeScript schemas, canonical workspace containment, Git-aware bounded search, central tool-and-path policy checks, cancellation, transient raw results, durable activity summaries, desktop inspection controls, tests, and ADR 0006.

items.title: Central permission engine
items.outcome: Every agent action is evaluated as allow, ask, or deny against a named resource.
acceptanceCriteria: Policies scope tool, command, path, network host, and extension resources.
Allow-once decisions never persist silently.
Denied actions execute no provider, filesystem, process, or network side effect.
Extensions cannot bypass policy evaluation.
items.changeNote: Completed in revision 0.8 with typed resource and origin rules, deterministic precedence, ephemeral allow-once grants, guarded execution, extension enforcement, tests, and ADR 0004.

items.title: File editing and real diff review
items.outcome: Users can inspect every agent change before accepting it.
acceptanceCriteria: Writes are workspace-bound, policy-checked, and recorded as artifacts.
Unified diff shows real changed files and hunks.
An interrupted write cannot leave an unreported partial state.
items.changeNote: Completed in revision 1.3 with bounded whole-file replacement, read-version preconditions, resource-bound allow-once policy, native confirmation, atomic Windows/Unix replacement, durable approval and safe diff metadata, and a transient real desktop diff view.

items.title: OS credential storage and redaction pipeline
items.outcome: Provider credentials survive safely without entering application data.
acceptanceCriteria: Credential Manager and the libsecret-compatible Linux Secret Service store opaque profile references.
Secret values are zeroized where practical.
Provider errors, diagnostics, exports, and crash reports pass central redaction tests.
items.changeNote: Completed in revision 1.4 with provider-bound opaque references, Windows Credential Manager and Linux Secret Service adapters, non-serializable zeroizing Rust secrets, central provider-error and persistence redaction, secure desktop onboarding, and cross-platform tests.

items.title: Provider diagnostics and capability discovery
items.outcome: A connection test explains exactly which behaviors a model endpoint supports.
acceptanceCriteria: Reachability, authentication, model discovery, streaming, and tool compatibility report separately.
The UI follows advertised capabilities instead of provider-name conditions.
Cloud gateway policy is explicit and warns before sending credentials to a custom origin.
items.changeNote: Includes the unresolved custom cloud-endpoint policy.

phases.title: Reliable task workspace
phases.outcome: Kiln supports concurrent daily work that survives restarts and preserves user changes.
exitGates: Two tasks can change one repository without sharing workspace or event state.
Restart during a turn produces a truthful recoverable task.
Restoring one checkpoint preserves unrelated user work.
Child processes and worktrees clean up after cancellation and restart.
Completed tasks retain verification evidence and a finalized diff.

items.title: Per-task Git worktrees and branches
items.outcome: Concurrent task changes remain isolated without claiming a security sandbox.
acceptanceCriteria: Create, recover, inspect, and clean task worktrees without deleting unrelated user data.
items.changeNote: Retained after direct-workspace H1 validation.

items.title: Concurrent task supervision
items.outcome: Multiple tasks run without interleaving events, approvals, output, or paths.
acceptanceCriteria: Ordered per-task queues and job ownership pass concurrency and fault-injection tests.
items.changeNote: No scope change.

items.title: Checkpoints, retry, fork, and targeted restore
items.outcome: Users can recover choices without rewriting unrelated work.
acceptanceCriteria: Checkpoint restore is auditable, scoped, and preserves unrelated user changes.
items.changeNote: No scope change.

items.title: Crash-resumable sessions
items.outcome: Application or adapter failure never fabricates completion or loses the durable task state.
acceptanceCriteria: Fault-injection restart tests produce explicit interrupted, recoverable, or completed receipts.
items.changeNote: No scope change.

items.title: Terminal and verification profiles
items.outcome: Tasks run explicit project checks with inspectable command output.
acceptanceCriteria: Shell selection, quoting, PTY lifecycle, process-tree cancellation, and verification receipts pass platform fixtures.
items.changeNote: No scope change.

items.title: Context compaction and usage visibility
items.outcome: Long sessions remain understandable and within provider limits.
acceptanceCriteria: Compaction boundaries are auditable and usage information degrades honestly by provider capability.
items.changeNote: No scope change.

phases.title: Open agent ecosystem
phases.outcome: Existing agents and external tools operate through Kiln's task, event, and permission surfaces.
exitGates: Goose and OpenCode sessions run through the same task interface.
Unsupported capabilities disable with an explanation.
MCP tools pass through the central permission engine.
A failed adapter restarts without restarting Kiln.
Exports can omit secrets and sensitive content.

items.title: MCP stdio and HTTP clients
items.outcome: Users can add typed tools without weakening central policy.
acceptanceCriteria: MCP lifecycle, health, schemas, calls, and approvals are represented as domain events.
items.changeNote: Begins only after the native permission path is proven.

items.title: ACP client and capability negotiation
items.outcome: Kiln can supervise compatible agents without provider-specific UI integrations.
acceptanceCriteria: Sessions, plans, tools, files, terminals, cancellation, and receipts map into Kiln events.
items.changeNote: Delayed until cancellation and recovery contracts are stable.

items.title: Goose and OpenCode profiles
items.outcome: Users can connect established agent runtimes through guided configuration.
acceptanceCriteria: One Goose and one OpenCode fixture complete through the common task interface.
items.changeNote: No bespoke task UI is permitted.

items.title: Sanitized session import and export
items.outcome: Users can move or share task evidence with explicit content controls.
acceptanceCriteria: A preview can omit secrets, source, command output, and provider payloads before export.
items.changeNote: No scope change.

phases.title: Windows and Linux beta
phases.outcome: A polished, installable daily driver for regular personal use.
exitGates: All core flows are keyboard accessible.
A 10,000-event session meets the agreed responsiveness budget.
A 24-hour task leaks neither processes nor unbounded memory.
Upgrade and rollback preserve sessions and policies.
Windows and Linux release smoke suites pass.

items.title: Installers, signing, and safe updates
items.outcome: Users can install, update, roll back, and remove Kiln predictably.
acceptanceCriteria: Signed release artifacts and update/rollback smoke tests pass on launch platforms.
items.changeNote: No scope change.

items.title: Keyboard, accessibility, and reduced motion
items.outcome: Core journeys remain operable without a pointer or animation.
acceptanceCriteria: Core workflows meet the documented WCAG 2.2 AA interaction expectations.
items.changeNote: No scope change.

items.title: Long-session performance and diagnostics
items.outcome: Large and long-running tasks stay responsive and explain failures safely.
acceptanceCriteria: Performance fixtures and redaction-preview diagnostic bundles pass release budgets.
items.changeNote: Combined related performance and support work.

items.title: Usage, cost, backup, and retention controls
items.outcome: Users understand provider consumption and control local history.
acceptanceCriteria: Usage degrades honestly and backup/retention operations are explicit and recoverable.

phases.timeframe: Deferred until the local product is stable

exitGates: Filesystem, network, CPU, memory, and execution-time limits are enforced and visible.
Remote pairing expires, revokes, and reconnects safely.

items.title: Platform process and filesystem containment
items.outcome: Autonomous jobs execute within documented OS-specific limits.
acceptanceCriteria: Containment boundaries and escape limitations have a dedicated security review.
items.changeNote: Deferred until local execution is reliable.

items.title: Headless daemon and authenticated pairing
items.outcome: A remote client can supervise without direct filesystem access.
acceptanceCriteria: Pairing, revocation, reconnect, and least-privilege APIs pass a separate threat model.

acceptanceCriteria: Physical-hardware release gates pass and remaining differences appear in-product.

phases.outcome: Kiln differentiates through understandable, policy-aware coordination rather than agent count.
exitGates: Every candidate has a user problem, success measure, and security model before commitment.

items.outcome: Users can understand dependencies, ownership, and evidence across collaborating agents.
acceptanceCriteria: Discovery defines when specialist graphs outperform one recoverable task loop.
items.changeNote: Not committed.

items.title: Model comparison and evaluation fixtures
items.outcome: Users can compare models on reproducible tasks without duplicating side effects.
acceptanceCriteria: Discovery defines isolation, evaluation measures, and cost controls.
items.changeNote: Not committed.

items.title: Reusable recipes and policy-aware review
items.outcome: Repeated engineering workflows become inspectable recipes rather than hidden automation.
acceptanceCriteria: Discovery defines authorship, trust, versioning, and rollback semantics.
items.changeNote: Not committed.

risks.risk: The desktop frontend is not yet proven from a clean dependency install.
risks.mitigation: Revision 1.2 proves clean hosted Windows and Ubuntu dependency installs, checks, production builds, and complete Rust workspace tests.

risks.risk: Future orchestration work could regress into the desktop transport layer.
risks.mitigation: The workspace now isolates core, providers, platform, and Git workspace contracts from kiln-tauri; keep Tauri-free dependency checks in CI.

risks.risk: Credentials and upstream payloads may leak without OS storage and centralized redaction.
risks.mitigation: H1-006 stores provider-bound opaque references in application data, keeps secret values in the OS vault, zeroizes Rust buffers where practical, and applies one tested redactor to provider errors and persistence boundaries.

risks.risk: Provider defaults and roadmap content can drift across Rust, web, desktop, and documentation.
risks.mitigation: H0-005 establishes generated roadmap outputs; provider-contract generation remains H1-007.

risks.risk: Windows works locally while Linux behavior remains an architectural claim.
risks.mitigation: Windows and Ubuntu quality jobs now pass on hosted runners and are both required before main can merge.

risks.risk: Concurrent writers or corrupt event order could make restart projections untruthful.
risks.mitigation: H0-008 uses one transactional SQLite writer, database uniqueness constraints, durable-tail checks, and validated ordered replay.

risks.risk: Provider bytes arriving after cancellation could rewrite a terminal turn or leave background work active.
risks.mitigation: H1-001 shares cancellation across HTTP and jobs, gives cancellation race priority, stops the channel at one terminal batch, and blocks late mutations in both projectors.

decisions.decision: Use a local-first Rust control plane with a Svelte/Tauri desktop client.
decisions.reason: The core must support desktop and future headless transports without duplicating orchestration.

decisions.decision: Whether cloud providers may use custom gateway origins.
decisions.reason: Gateway flexibility must not make credential destination ambiguous.

decisions.decision: Whether Rig becomes the native loop implementation or remains architectural inspiration.
decisions.reason: Adoption should follow a stable event, tool, and provider contract.

decisions.decision: Which Linux package formats receive first-class support.
decisions.reason: Packaging investment should follow tested user distribution needs.

decisions.decision: Use versioned, causally ordered application events as the interface and replay boundary.
decisions.reason: Provider payloads and transport behavior must not become the product state model.

decisions.decision: Use SQLite as an immutable local event log with one H0 writer.
decisions.reason: Kiln needs transactional restart and replay without requiring an external service.

decisions.decision: Route every native and extension action through one guarded permission engine.
decisions.reason: Allow, ask, deny, and ephemeral approval semantics must not vary by transport or tool source.

decisions.decision: Normalize provider SSE behind ordered Tauri channels and one shared cancellation domain.
decisions.reason: Streaming must remain provider-independent, durable before display, and immune to late cancellation races.

decisions.decision: Require native confirmation and optimistic version checks for atomic direct-workspace edits.
decisions.reason: A frontend assertion must not grant write access, stale reads must not overwrite user work, and completed edits need durable review evidence.

decisions.decision: Store provider secrets in OS credential services and transport only provider-bound opaque references.
decisions.reason: Normal application data and frontend provider commands must not expose durable secret values, and every output boundary needs one tested redaction contract.

changeLog.summary: Completed OS credential storage and centralized secret redaction.
changes: Added provider-bound opaque credential profiles backed by Windows Credential Manager and the Linux Secret Service, with serialized blocking access and replacement cleanup.
Removed raw credentials from normal frontend test and chat payloads, resolved references only inside the trusted Rust desktop boundary, and restored stored profile references at startup.
Made Rust secrets non-serializable and zeroizing on drop, while documenting the limits of JavaScript and upstream-library memory handling.

Applied one dynamic and structural redactor to provider errors and the SQLite persistence gate, with tests covering diagnostics, exports, crash text, injected raw credentials, and cross-provider reference misuse.
Completed H1-006, mitigated the credential-leak risk, accepted ADR 0008, and moved provider diagnostics and capability discovery to the active focus.

changeLog.summary: Completed native-confirmed file editing and real diff review.
changes: Added typed read hashes and bounded write_file requests with required optimistic concurrency for existing UTF-8 files.
Bound allow-once grants to the approved origin and exact resource, blocked Git metadata and symbolic-link replacement, and required a Rust-owned native confirmation.
Implemented synchronized same-directory temporary writes with atomic Windows and Unix replacement plus cancellation before the filesystem transition.
Recorded approval, safe tool summaries, and diff artifact metadata in causal order while keeping full diffs transient, and added a real desktop edit and diff-review surface.
Completed H1-005 and moved credential storage and provider diagnostics to the active focus.

changeLog.summary: Closed the cross-platform foundation gates and protected the public main branch.
changes: Forced byte-checked generated artifacts to stable LF checkout semantics and made the SQLite projection snapshot compare structured JSON instead of platform line endings.
Passed the complete hosted quality workflow on Windows and Ubuntu, including generated fixtures, web and desktop builds, formatting, Clippy, and all Rust tests.
Protected main behind pull requests, current-branch checks, resolved review conversations, and force-push and deletion prevention.
Marked the reproducible desktop build and Windows/Linux CI items complete, closed their platform risks, and moved the active roadmap horizon to H1.

changeLog.summary: Completed real Git project selection and removed the desktop dependency-install blocker.
changes: Added the Tauri-free kiln-workspace crate with canonical-root discovery, path-derived identity, branch and commit projection, porcelain-v2 status parsing, ownership checks, disabled hooks and filesystem monitors, bounded output, and a 15-second inspection limit.

Persisted project_opened and workspace_ready events before activation, derived recent projects from immutable SQLite history, and revalidated remembered roots at startup without storing credentials or remote URLs.

Added typed Rust and TypeScript project projections plus a desktop picker that shows branch, truthful working-tree state, recent availability, and actionable invalid-selection errors while blocking turns without a repository.
Generated desktop/package-lock.json, aligned the official Svelte Vite plugin with Vite 8, migrated production minification to Oxc, and passed a clean Windows npm ci, Svelte check, and desktop build.
Added real temporary-Git, storage, transport, projection, and credential-shape tests plus the project/workspace guide; read-only file and search tools are next.

changeLog.summary: Completed normalized provider streaming and cancellation from HTTP frames to durable desktop projection.
changes: Added OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages, and compatible local SSE parsers with normalized delta, completion, and cancellation events.
Added a shared cancellation domain that drops active HTTP and job futures and gives cancellation priority over queued late frames.
Streamed normalized events through a typed Tauri channel, converted them to application events, and committed each batch before Svelte projection.
Added a desktop stop control, duplicate-turn protection, terminal channel handling, and late-mutation guards in Rust and TypeScript.
Added protocol, framing, cancellation, registry, bridge, and projection tests plus the streaming guide and ADR 0005; repository selection is next.

changeLog.summary: Completed the central permission engine before introducing repository tools.
changes: Added typed tool, command, path, network-host, and extension resources with task, project, provider-profile, and global policy targets.
Defined deterministic target, origin, resource, and deny/ask/allow precedence with an ask-by-default fallback.
Kept allow-once grants outside serializable rules and consumed them at the guarded execution boundary.
Proved denied native and extension-origin actions invoke no side-effect closure, documented the trust boundary, and accepted ADR 0004.
Started H1-001 streaming and cancellation while H0 desktop dependency and hosted CI gates remain open.

changeLog.summary: Completed the recorded-session integration gate and established the Windows/Linux quality workflow.
changes: Added one canonical 25-event fake session covering streaming, planning, approval, tool output, a diff, tests, and a final receipt.
Generated the Svelte recording from JSON and verified deterministic task and inspector projections against a Rust snapshot.
Added a Windows and Ubuntu GitHub Actions matrix with web, Svelte, Rust, freshness, lint, and build gates.
Added executable fixtures for spaces, Unicode paths, mixed line endings, and process cancellation; H0-010 remains active until hosted runs and required checks are confirmed.
Marked H0-004 blocked because the approval service still rejects the registry request needed to create the desktop lockfile.

changeLog.summary: Completed restart-safe SQLite integration from Tauri startup through the Svelte projection.
changes: Initialized kiln.db under the Tauri application-data directory and exposed typed append/load commands.
Added a durable desktop history coordinator that commits event batches before projection and resets its sequencer after failed writes.
Restored the ordered task stream and deterministic projection before enabling the desktop composer.
Added durability coordinator tests and marked H0-008 complete; recorded fake-session replay and CI are next.

changeLog.summary: Started durable SQLite event storage behind a Tauri-free crate.
changes: Added storage schema version 1 with indexed immutable event envelopes and explicit migration history.
Implemented one-stream transactional append, durable-tail sequence checks, and validated replay.
Added persistence-time credential-marker rejection plus atomicity, rollback, migration, file reopen, and projection-snapshot tests.
Documented the physical schema, recovery rules, safety boundary, and ADR 0003; H0-008 remains in progress for desktop append/startup integration.

changeLog.summary: Completed the versioned application-event boundary from Rust through the Svelte projection.
changes: Added message lifecycle events and stable camel-case transport fields to the Rust contract.
Replaced direct Svelte conversation and activity mutation with deterministic ordered-event projections.
Converted provider success and failure results into message and receipt events at the desktop bridge.
Added cross-language contract checks, replay tests, complete contract documentation, and ADR 0002.

changeLog.summary: Extracted the Tauri-free Rust foundation and started the versioned application event contract.
changes: Created a Cargo workspace with kiln-core, kiln-providers, kiln-platform, and a thin kiln-tauri shell.
Moved provider fixtures and normalized contracts out of the desktop transport.
Added versioned command and event envelopes with causal stream ordering and forward-compatible field handling.
Marked H0-006 done and H0-007 in progress after workspace and isolated-core tests passed.

changeLog.summary: Converted the roadmap into a generated source of truth and incorporated the foundation review.
changes: Prioritized a reproducible desktop build, Rust core extraction, event contract, SQLite replay, and CI.
Required permissions before repository tools and streaming before ecosystem integrations.
Added risk, decision, metric, and change-history records.
Synchronized web and desktop roadmap summaries from the structured source.

changeLog.summary: Established the initial H0–H7 product roadmap.
changes: Set Windows and Linux as launch platforms.
Deferred macOS support and secure remote operation until release gates are met.
